newsitem.title: GERMANY: German opposition alarmed over Bonn defying Buba.
newsitem.headline: German opposition alarmed over Bonn defying Buba.

text.p: Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD) said on Wednesday they were alarmed at the government's plans to defy the will of the Bundesbank and revalue the central bank's gold and currency reserves.
Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier, the SPD's parliamentary financial expert, told Germany's ARD television that the government was damaging the Bundesbank's reputation with its "hectic efforts to reduce debts".

The Bundesbank issued a strongly worded rejection of Finance Minister Theo Waigel's plans to raise extra cash by revaluing the assets. The government coalition quickly responded by saying it would proceed with its plans regardless.

"I am very alarmed about the course of events," Matthaeus-Maier said in an interview on Germany's main evening news broadcast. "That is a break in the decade-long tradition of stability, against the will of the Bundesbank, a hectic effort to reduce debts by grabbing the gold treasure."
Matthaeus-Maier said the plans were damaging to the Bundesbank.

"It damages the reputation of the Bundesbank, the guarantee of our stability, and it damages our reputation around the world because we are giving the appearance we are fiddling the accounts," she said.
